reference.text: Clinicians should initiate glycemic management protocols and procedures to treat persistent hyperglycemia, >= 10 mmol/L (180 mg/dL) in critically ill adults
Clinicians should use glycemic management protocols and procedures that demonstrate a low risk of hypoglycemia among critically ill adults and should treat hypoglycemia without delay
Based on available RCT data, in critically ill adults, we 'suggest against' titrating an insulin infusion to a lower BG target INT 4.4-7.7 mmol/L vs CONV 7.8-11.1 mmol/L
Research statement: we recommend high-quality interventional trials of individualized glycemic targets in critically ill adults, stratified by prior glycemic control
We 'suggest' using continuous IV insulin infusion rather than intermittent subcutaneous insulin in the acute management of hyperglycemia in critically ill adults
We 'suggest' frequent (<= 1 hr, continuous or near-continuous) glucose monitoring vs intervals > hourly in critically ill adults on IV insulin during glycemic instability
We 'suggest' use of a protocol that includes explicit decision support tools over a protocol with no such tools in critically ill adults receiving IV insulin infusions
Clinicians should initiate glycemic management protocols and procedures to treat persistent hyperglycemia, >= 10 mmol/L in critically ill children
Clinicians should use glycemic management protocols and procedures that demonstrate a low risk of hypoglycemia among critically ill children and should treat hypoglycemia without delay
We 'recommend against' INT BG control 4.4-7.7 mmol/L vs CONV 7.8-11.1 mmol/L in critically ill children
We make 'no recommendation' regarding continuous IV insulin infusion over intermittent SC insulin in critically ill pediatric patients; 'in our practice' IV infusion is used
We make 'no recommendation' regarding frequent (<= 1 hr) vs less frequent BG monitoring in pediatric patients on insulin infusion; 'in our practice' frequent monitoring
We 'suggest' use of explicit decision support tools over no such tools in critically ill pediatric patients receiving IV insulin infusions
Research statement: we strongly recommend high-quality research on explicit decision support tools for insulin infusion titration in pediatric patients
Recommendation: The panel is unable to provide a specific statement (POC device vs central lab/blood gas analyzer for BG monitoring) due to inconsistent methodologies

notes: Reference = Table 3 Summary of Recommendations (p.5), clean text; matches abstract counts (adults: 2 GPS, 4 conditional, 1 research; peds: 2 GPS, 1 strong, 1 conditional, 2 'in our practice', 1 research). Research statements counted as ungraded (best_practice bucket per task definition); 'no recommendation / in our practice' as no_recommendation. Added one body-only ungraded item: POC device question 'panel is unable to provide a specific statement' (p.13) as no_recommendation. None of the 9 ungraded items was extracted.
